note: Monthly snapshot. Not a live feed.

endo.title: Aberdeen-led £2.3m trial will test a personalised endometriosis pain programme
endo.description: NIHR is funding a five-year University of Aberdeen and NHS Grampian study of a 12-week endometriosis-specific pain management programme (e-PMP), combining medication review, physiotherapy, and psychological support against standard care.
endo.author: BBC News

endo.title: WSU team reports a single-dose nanotherapy that shrank endometriosis lesions in mice
endo.description: Washington State University researchers delivered niclosamide on a dendrimer to an endometriosis-associated immune cell. In a mouse model, one injection reduced lesion size and number and pain sensitivity. Results are in Advanced Healthcare Materials; human trials are not yet underway.
endo.author: Washington State University

endo.title: Yale study links IL-16 and lesion gene patterns to endometriosis pain
endo.description: Biopsies from symptomatic and asymptomatic endometriosis showed genetic differences tied to pain, including higher IL-16. The Sept. 10 Molecular Human Reproduction paper offers a molecular clue for why lesion burden and pain severity often do not match.
endo.author: Yale School of Medicine

endo.title: Edinburgh group finds an androgen fingerprint that flagged endometriosis in blood
endo.description: University of Edinburgh scientists compared 159 women with confirmed endometriosis and 57 without. Higher 11-ketotestosterone and a broader 11-oxygenated androgen pattern identified more than 95 percent of cases in this sample. A commercial blood test is not yet available.
endo.author: Bioscience Today

endo.title: NIH Trailblazer award backs University of Florida quantum sensors for early endometriosis
endo.description: Engineering professor Laura Kim received a three-year NIH Trailblazer Award to build a diamond-based quantum sensing platform meant to read faint magnetic signals in tissue, with early-stage endometriosis as the first clinical target.
endo.author: University of Florida / News-Medical

endo.title: Monash team funded to pursue a non-hormonal NPSR1 blocker for endometriosis pain
endo.description: MedChem Australia awarded more than A$415,000 for 12 months to develop compounds against neuropeptide S receptor 1, expressed on inflammatory cells in peritoneal fluid. Mouse work linked receptor blockade to less pelvic pain and lower TNF-alpha.
endo.author: Monash University

endo.title: Patients and doctors question surgery-plus-hormones as a lasting fix
endo.description: A Guardian report on NHS care cites patients whose pain relief after surgery and hormonal suppression was short-lived, alongside a study finding the usual dual approach did not improve quality of life for chronic pelvic pain.
endo.author: The Guardian

endo.title: EndoFound publishes a back-to-school guide on endometriosis in teens
endo.description: The Endometriosis Foundation of America walks through teen symptoms, why period pain that disrupts school is not normal, and the 7-to-10-year diagnostic delay that often starts in adolescence.
endo.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

womens.title: ‘It makes you feel helpless’: standard endometriosis care under scrutiny
womens.description: Natalie Greenwood and other patients describe repeated surgery and chemical menopause that only briefly ease pain. Clinicians quoted in the piece say quality-of-life gains from the usual NHS pathway are limited.
womens.author: The Guardian

womens.title: Powers Health opens a chronic pelvic pain pathway aimed at cutting the diagnostic delay
womens.description: An Indiana program led by OB/GYN Osama Zaghmout routes pelvic pain patients to exam, pelvic-floor physical therapy, MRI, and colorectal referral when bowel disease is suspected. The clinic cites the typical 7-to-10-year wait for an endometriosis diagnosis.
womens.author: Powers Health

womens.title: First UK trial of a remote endometriosis pain programme gets NIHR backing
womens.description: ITV reports the Aberdeen e-PMP trial will compare a 12-week remote package — CBT-informed therapy, specialist physiotherapy, intimacy and communication support, and medication optimisation — with standard care alone.
womens.author: ITV News

womens.title: How endometriosis pain varies: Yale highlights a symptom-severity mismatch
womens.description: Yale School of Medicine summarizes patient biopsies showing inflammatory signals, including IL-16, that track with pain even when visible disease is limited. About 190 million people worldwide live with the condition.
womens.author: Yale School of Medicine

womens.title: Two-year relugolix combination data show sustained endometriosis pain response
womens.description: A Contemporary OB/GYN panel reviews the SPIRIT open-label extension: at two years, 85 percent met the dysmenorrhea responder threshold and 74 percent the non-menstrual pelvic pain threshold, with no new safety signal reported.
womens.author: Contemporary OB/GYN

womens.title: Teen endometriosis guide: pain that cancels school is a reason to be seen
womens.description: EndoFound’s September guide covers bowel and bladder symptoms, fatigue, and why ‘you will grow out of it’ delays care, especially for teens of color.
womens.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

womens.title: Team EndoStrong expands to 70 runners at the 2026 New York City Marathon
womens.description: New York Road Runners increased EndoFound’s marathon slots by 40 percent. The team hopes to top $400,000 after raising nearly $300,000 in 2025 for awareness, education, and research.
womens.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

womens.title: Charlotte McCann left her career at 27 because endometriosis pain was unmanageable
womens.description: BBC profiles a patient symptomatic since age 14 who is watching the Aberdeen pain-programme trial as a possible option for people whose surgery and medication have not held.
womens.author: BBC News

fertility.title: EndoFound review: endometrioma surgery can cut ovarian reserve; preserve eggs first when possible
fertility.description: An EndoNews summary of fertility-preservation evidence reports AMH drops of about 39.5 percent after unilateral cystectomy and 57 percent after bilateral surgery, and a 51.7 percent lower mature-oocyte yield when preservation followed prior endometrioma surgery.
fertility.author: EndoNews / Endometriosis Foundation of America

fertility.title: Hysteroscopy before first frozen transfer linked to higher pregnancy rates in endometriosis
fertility.description: A Frontiers in Medicine cohort found polyps and chronic endometritis were common in endometriosis-related infertility. After matching, clinical pregnancy was 67.5 percent with pre-FET hysteroscopy versus 42.5 percent without.
fertility.author: Frontiers in Medicine

fertility.title: Ovarian endometriosis, not all subtypes, tracked with lower reserve and embryo quality
fertility.description: Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics (10 June 2026) found lower antral follicle counts and fewer mature oocytes in ovarian endometriosis than in peritoneal disease, and argued for earlier elective egg freezing in that subtype.
fertility.author: Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics

fertility.title: Non-hormonal drug work matters for people who cannot stay on cycle suppression
fertility.description: Monash investigators note that current hormonal drugs suppress the cycle, forcing a choice between pain control and trying to conceive. Their NPSR1 program is explicitly non-hormonal.
fertility.author: Monash University

fertility.title: Tissue-sparing surgery and oocyte freezing are the practical levers in the new EndoFound review
fertility.description: The same September review finds oocyte cryopreservation the most established option, with ovarian-tissue freezing and in-vitro maturation still short of endometriosis-specific evidence. CO2 laser and plasma approaches may spare more ovary than stripping, but technique choice is not settled.
fertility.author: EndoNews

fertility.title: After excision for stage IV disease, one patient conceived twice without IVF
fertility.description: EndoFound’s May profile of Bryn Jones describes five miscarriages, a four-hour stage IV excision in 2022, and later unassisted births in 2024 and 2025. A single story, not a fertility protocol.
fertility.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

fertility.title: Relugolix combination’s contraceptive effect is being tracked alongside pain data
fertility.description: Panelists discussing two-year SPIRIT extension results also flagged the SERINE study of contraceptive efficacy for relugolix combination therapy, with fuller data expected at ASRM this fall. People planning pregnancy need a different regimen.
fertility.author: Contemporary OB/GYN

medical.title: Nanoparticle niclosamide reduced lesions after one dose in a mouse endometriosis model
medical.description: Kanako Hayashi and colleagues targeted a disease-associated immune cell with a dendrimer-niclosamide construct. Published in Advanced Healthcare Materials; the group is seeking a path to human testing.
medical.author: Washington State University

medical.title: Molecular Human Reproduction: IL-16 elevation tracked with painful endometriosis
medical.description: Ramanaiah Mamillapalli and colleagues report that IL-16 may recruit immune cells into lesions and amplify other cytokines. Findings published 10 September 2026.
medical.author: Yale School of Medicine

medical.title: 11-oxygenated androgens distinguished endometriosis in an Edinburgh blood study
medical.description: The group is working with Edinburgh Innovations to find a partner for a diagnostic based on 11-ketotestosterone and related androgens. Surgical confirmation remains the current reference standard.
medical.author: Bioscience Today

medical.title: NIH funds a quantum-sensing approach to early endometriosis detection
medical.description: University of Florida’s Laura Kim will adapt diamond quantum sensors to read microscopic magnetic signals in tissue. The three-year Trailblazer award treats endometriosis as the first women’s-health application.
medical.author: University of Florida

medical.title: NPSR1 named as a genetically backed, non-hormonal drug target
medical.description: Thomas Tapmeier, Celine Valant, Trang Pham, and Beverley Vollenhoven received MedChem Australia funding to advance NPSR1 compounds after mouse data showed less pain and lower TNF-alpha.
medical.author: Monash University

medical.title: SPIRIT extension: relugolix combination responses held from week 52 to week 104
medical.description: Dysmenorrhea response 85 percent and non-menstrual pelvic pain response 74 percent at two years. Headache, nasopharyngitis, and hot flushes were the common adverse events; further bone loss was uncommon in the discussion.
medical.author: Contemporary OB/GYN

medical.title: NIHR trial will test whether multidisciplinary pain care beats usual endometriosis treatment
medical.description: Lucky Saraswat at NHS Grampian is leading the e-PMP study. Investigators note pain returns in up to half of people after surgery, which is why the trial targets those not controlled by surgery or medication alone.
medical.author: ITV News

medical.title: StatPearls endometriosis chapter updated June 2026
medical.description: The NCBI review restates endometriosis as an estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease with pelvic pain and infertility as the main clinical features, and prevalence up to 35–50 percent among people with chronic pelvic pain or infertility.
medical.author: StatPearls / NCBI

heartwarming.title: Law student Isabelle Garino pushed for surgery and says she feels the best she has in a decade
heartwarming.description: EndoFound’s 25 September profile: after years of dismissed bleeding and pain, Garino was scheduled for excision within months of a specialist visit. Surgeons found pelvic disease and pooled blood; six months later she is back in class and headed to a law job.
heartwarming.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

heartwarming.title: Haley’s stage IV excision found nearly 50 lesions imaging had missed for 17 years
heartwarming.description: A September patient account from ESSE Care: spring 2026 excision removed deep disease, fibroids, and five endometriomas and repaired ovaries. Three months later she reports new food tolerance, less nerve pain, and clearer thinking. She does not call it a cure.
heartwarming.author: ESSE Care

heartwarming.title: Abbie Hixson is running the New York City Marathon to talk about the surgery she wished someone had named
heartwarming.description: After excision in April 2025, Hixson joined Team EndoStrong with family. The 2026 squad has 70 slots and a fundraising goal above $400,000.
heartwarming.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

heartwarming.title: Charlotte McCann, symptomatic since 14, is hoping the Aberdeen pain trial helps people who had to leave work
heartwarming.description: BBC’s 30 September story pairs a patient’s lost career with the start of a funded pain-management study she hopes will reach others in the same place.
heartwarming.author: BBC News

heartwarming.title: A Powers Health pelvic-pain patient calls the new program path ‘miraculous’
heartwarming.description: The 21 September clinic story pairs a patient account with a shorter route from pelvic pain to physical therapy, imaging, and surgical referral instead of another decade of dismissal.
heartwarming.author: Powers Health

heartwarming.title: Endo Excision for All patients describe getting back to work, workouts, and meals after funded surgery
heartwarming.description: The nonprofit’s story page includes 2026 recoveries: one person operated on 11 February who could eat and walk again within two months, and another whose surgery was completed 13 May after an insurance fight.
heartwarming.author: Endo Excision for All

heartwarming.title: After five miscarriages and stage IV excision, Bryn Jones had two children
heartwarming.description: EndoFound, 15 May 2026: Jones was told there was no chance of endometriosis, then had a four-hour excision. Food reactions eased and she later gave birth to a son in 2024 and a daughter in 2025.
heartwarming.author: Endometriosis Foundation of America

heartwarming.title: Natalie Greenwood keeps naming what surgery did not fix
heartwarming.description: Greenwood tells The Guardian she is non-functioning much of the time from fatigue, and that repeated operations have not been a lasting fix. The piece is a patient record of limits, not a recovery ad.
heartwarming.author: The Guardian
